_what: The company's visual identity, in one file, because it was in three and they had already drifted. Extracted from https://relevant.software/ on 2026-09-16 by reading the site's own :root custom properties and computed styles rather than by eye. Every consumer renders FROM this: the HTML report, the calibration report, the estimate workbook and the plan's Gantt. Change a colour here and it changes everywhere, which is the point.

source.how: Playwright: document.styleSheets :root custom properties, plus getComputedStyle over the rendered page for the type scale and the colours actually in use.
source.why_not_eyedropped: A screenshot samples what a JPEG encoder decided. The site publishes its own tokens; those are the brand, and they carry the names the company's own front end uses.

font.css_family: "PP Mori", "PP Mori Fallback", Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif
font.css_family_why: The CSS stack names the metric-adjusted fallback face declared beside it, so a reader without PP Mori gets Arial sized to PP Mori's metrics rather than Arial at its own. Plain `Arial` is kept last for a browser that ignores the @font-face.
font.why: PP Mori is the brand face — a licensed Pangram Pangram font, self-hosted on the site behind hashed build URLs. It cannot be embedded in a document we hand a client, and linking the site's own woff2 would break the moment the page is opened offline or the build hash rotates. So: use it where the reader has it installed, and fall back to Arial, which is what the site itself falls back to.

metric_overrides.why: Copied from the site's own "fontPPMori Fallback" face. They make Arial occupy the same space PP Mori would, so a document laid out for one does not reflow into the other.

font.xlsx_family_why: Excel cannot load a webfont, and a workbook naming a font the reader lacks is silently re-substituted per machine. Arial is present on every platform Excel runs on, so the sheet looks the same everywhere.

palette._what: Names are roles, not colours, so a document never hardcodes a hex. The `light` set is the definition; `dark` overrides only what has to move.
palette.dark_why: The site ships no dark theme, so this half is derived rather than extracted and is labelled as such. The brand navy is unreadable on a dark ground, so it is lifted to a tint of itself that holds the same hue at usable contrast; the neutrals are the site's ink and ground inverted through the same relationship. Nothing here claims to be the company's dark palette — it claims to be this one, legible at night.

roles._what: One colour per delivery role, used by the Gantt so a reader can tell who is doing what without reading a label. Derived from the brand navy by rotating hue and holding saturation, so the chart reads as one family rather than as a highlighter set.
roles._contrast: Every one of these carries white text at 14px and clears WCAG AA against #ffffff. Bars are filled at full strength and idle cells at brand_tint, so occupancy is visible in greyscale and in print.

type_scale._what: The site's clamp() scale, flattened to the sizes a document actually uses.
